title: Totally Honest
tagline: The campaign that dared a century-old brand to tell the truth.
pullQuote: What if the most powerful thing Colgate could say was: we’re not perfect — and neither are you.
copy: For too long, oral care advertising had shown us impossibly white smiles in impossibly pristine settings. We pitched something radical: show real teeth, in real moments, belonging to real people. Totally Honest launched across digital, OOH, and broadcast — and immediately became the most-talked-about oral care campaign of the year.

Three months in, product sales grew 18% year-over-year. Social engagement outpaced category benchmarks by 4×. But more than the numbers, Colgate had done something it hadn’t done in decades — it had made people feel something.

title: Be Iconic
tagline: Reclaiming the word iconic for the brand that invented it.
pullQuote: Luxury isn’t inherited. It’s earned — one statement at a time.
copy: Cadillac had a legacy problem: everyone knew the name, but nobody under 45 cared. Our brief was to make Cadillac feel inevitable again — not through nostalgia, but through sheer presence. Be Iconic was a statement of intent as much as an advertising campaign, built around film, digital, and a refreshed brand voice sharp enough to cut through an increasingly crowded luxury market.

Launched with a 90-second brand film and an integrated digital campaign across Canada and the US, Be Iconic drove a 23% increase in brand consideration among 35–49 year-old luxury car shoppers. The film went on to be shortlisted at Cannes Lions.

title: Reconnecting New York
tagline: Twenty years later, a city needed to remember together — not alone.
pullQuote: The most powerful memorial isn’t built in stone. It’s built in the spaces between people.
copy: In the weeks leading up to the twentieth anniversary of September 11th, we were briefed on something quietly ambitious: build a digital experience that would help people reconnect on September 12th — the day after. Not a day of grief, but the day ordinary New Yorkers turned to each other.

We created an interactive platform where users could share a memory, a message, or a moment of quiet with a stranger across the city. Over 400,000 people participated across 72 hours. The experience was featured in The New York Times and recognized by the International Emmy Foundation for its impact.

title: Recent Web Sites
tagline: Screens that move people. Sites that do things no site has done before.
pullQuote: Every pixel is a decision. Every decision is a chance to do something no one has seen yet.
copy: Across twenty-five years we’ve built websites for some of the world’s most demanding brands — launches that had to be perfect on day one, platforms built to handle millions of visitors, and experiences designed to shift how people feel about a product before they ever touch it. This is a selection of recent work that doesn’t fit neatly into a single campaign or category.

From luxury automotive configurators to non-profit advocacy platforms, from e-commerce flagships to interactive brand worlds, our digital work is defined by one principle: the technology should be invisible. What the visitor feels is all that matters.

title: Social Change
tagline: We gave grassroots advocates a voice loud enough to reach Parliament Hill.
pullQuote: Real change doesn’t start with policy. It starts with a story someone can’t stop thinking about.
copy: Bedtime Stories for Social Change is a Canadian non-profit that uses narrative — film, audio, and illustrated storytelling — to drive awareness and advocacy around issues that traditional campaigns can’t crack. They came to us to help amplify their content, build a digital presence that matched the power of their stories, and launch a fundraising campaign that felt as human as the work itself.

Over six months, we redesigned their digital platform, produced a content series featuring advocates from across the country, and ran a social campaign that drove a 210% increase in monthly donors. The work was recognized at the Canadian Marketing Awards and became a case study in purpose-driven digital strategy.

title: Poster for Everyone
tagline: Accessibility isn’t a feature. It’s the whole point.
pullQuote: Art has always been for everyone. We just needed to make the poster catch up.
copy: The Rick Hansen Foundation has spent decades advocating for a world without barriers. When they wanted to bring that message to a new generation, they came to us with a brief about public art — specifically, how to make iconic Canadian imagery fully accessible to people with visual impairments. Poster for Everyone combined tactile printing, audio descriptions, and an AR layer so that every person, regardless of ability, could experience the same cultural moment.

Deployed in transit stations, galleries, and schools across Canada, the campaign generated national media coverage and became one of the most-shared RHF campaigns in their history. The accessible poster format was subsequently adopted by three provincial arts councils as a permanent standard.

title: Sweat Machine
tagline: We turned the science of sweat into something nobody had ever seen.
pullQuote: Sweat is honest. It doesn’t lie about effort.
copy: Gatorade wanted to own the conversation around athletic performance — not just refreshment. Sweat Machine was an interactive digital platform and physical installation that transformed real-time athlete data (heart rate, temperature, sweat output) into generative visual art. Every athlete became their own masterpiece.

Launched at Toronto’s Harbourfront Centre during the Pan Am Games, Sweat Machine drew over 12,000 visitors in four days and generated 40M+ social impressions. The digital platform ran for six months and became a permanent fixture of Gatorade’s D2C strategy.

title: ComplexCon
tagline: When culture shows up, you don’t just show up — you show out.
pullQuote: We didn’t build a booth. We built a moment.
copy: ComplexCon is where sneaker culture, streetwear, music, and art converge. For Adidas, we designed an activation that didn’t feel like advertising — it felt like an event within the event. Custom architecture, a live DJ setup, an exclusive drop, and a social photo moment that drove 28K UGC posts over the weekend.
The activation was named Best Brand Experience at ComplexCon 2022 and drove a 14% lift in brand preference among 18–28 year-old males in the US — the most elusive demographic in the category.

title: Cadillac XT4
tagline: The smallest Cadillac ever built. Every inch of it, iconic.
pullQuote: Luxury doesn’t have to be large. It has to be undeniable.
copy: Launching a compact SUV under a brand synonymous with full-size luxury is a delicate brief. The Cadillac XT4 needed to feel premium without feeling like a compromise — and it needed to reach a buyer who had never considered Cadillac before. We built a launch campaign that leaned into the tension: small, but not lesser. Urban, but not ordinary.

The digital-first campaign ran across Canada and select US markets, anchored by a launch film that showed the XT4 navigating city environments no traditional Cadillac had ever belonged in. First-year sales exceeded forecast by 22%, with first-time Cadillac buyers accounting for 61% of XT4 purchases.

title: Nuit Blanche
tagline: An all-night art festival became the world’s most beautiful skincare ad.
pullQuote: Beauty isn’t a product. It’s what happens when art touches science.
copy: Nuit Blanche gave us the ultimate brief: occupy a piece of downtown Toronto for one night and make people fall in love with Shiseido’s newest skincare collection. We built an immersive installation called Future Skin — a large-scale LED environment where visitors’ faces were scanned and rendered in real-time as luminous, abstract portraits.

Over 8,000 people experienced Future Skin across the night. The installation was covered by Vogue, WWD, and Wallpaper*, generating 15M+ organic impressions across social. The product collection sold out within 48 hours of the campaign launch.

title: Tenor Takeover
tagline: We gave Canada’s most beloved bread brand a voice it never knew it had.
pullQuote: The best brand moments don’t feel like advertising. They feel like something you stumbled into and can’t stop smiling about.
copy: D’Italiano bread has been on Canadian tables for generations. The challenge was to make it feel exciting to a younger demographic without alienating the loyal base who grew up with it. The insight: food brings people together, and nothing brings people together quite like an unexpected, joyful spectacle. Tenor Takeover surprised unsuspecting shoppers in grocery stores across Canada with operatic flash mob performances celebrating everyday mealtime moments.

The stunts were filmed and released as a multi-part social series, driving 18M organic views across YouTube and Instagram in the first month. The campaign became D’Italiano’s most-shared content ever and won Gold at the Marketing Awards for Best Social Campaign.

title: Chase The Gear
tagline: We turned gear-hunting into a city-wide game.
pullQuote: The best retail experience isn’t in the store. It’s the reason you run to get there.
copy: Sport Chek needed a back-to-school campaign that would cut through the noise in a category full of performance claims and celebrity endorsements. Our idea: make the gear itself worth chasing. Chase the Gear was a city-wide scavenger hunt built on a custom mobile platform, hiding limited-edition gear drops at locations revealed through social clues, AR markers, and real-time leaderboards.

Running across six Canadian cities over three weeks, Chase the Gear drove 85,000 app downloads, 2.3M social impressions, and a 34% lift in Sport Chek app purchases during the campaign period. It became the brand’s highest-performing digital activation to date.

title: Go Further
tagline: A truck brand with a bigger idea: you can always go further.
pullQuote: Canadians don’t want to be sold to. They want to be challenged.
copy: Ford needed to reconnect with Canadian truck buyers who had started looking elsewhere. Our insight was simple: the truck is a tool, but what it enables is a life without limits. Go Further was less a product campaign and more a call to action — to the adventurer, the entrepreneur, the builder who never settles.

The campaign launched with a 60-second film shot across five provinces and was supported by a digital content series featuring real Canadians doing extraordinary things in their Ford trucks. Dealer visits increased 19% over the campaign period. Ford F-Series remained the best-selling vehicle in Canada for the 14th consecutive year.

title: MiO POV
tagline: Hydration, your way. We made water personal.
pullQuote: The product was always the point of view. We just built the world around it.
copy: MiO had a product story nobody was telling right: this tiny bottle lets you flavour your water exactly how you want it, anywhere. The brief was to make personalization feel visceral rather than clinical — to show the world through the eyes of someone who refuses to accept the default. MiO POV was a first-person content platform built around athlete, artist, and creator perspectives, each one as distinctive as the flavours themselves.

Produced across eight creator partnerships and distributed natively across TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts, MiO POV drove a 44% increase in brand engagement among 18–34 year-olds and became the template for Kraft Heinz’s creator content strategy in Canada.

title: Bachelor Experience
tagline: The most dramatic ring moment in television history — and we built it.
pullQuote: When thirty million people are watching, the ring has to be perfect. Everything else can be reality TV.
copy: Michael Hill came to us with a brief that was equal parts thrilling and terrifying: design and produce the engagement ring reveal for the finale of The Bachelor Canada, live on national television. The ring would be seen by over two million viewers the night of the finale and another 30M+ through international syndication and social sharing. It needed to be flawless — and it needed to feel like Michael Hill, not like a prop.

We designed the reveal experience in collaboration with the show’s production team, built a custom display environment for the final rose ceremony, and produced a behind-the-scenes content series that ran across Michael Hill’s social platforms leading up to the finale. Website traffic increased 380% during the finale week, with the engagement ring selling out within 48 hours of broadcast.

title: Augmented Reality
tagline: We put the new Volkswagen in every driveway in Canada before a single car shipped.
pullQuote: The future of the test drive isn’t at the dealership. It’s wherever you are right now.
copy: Volkswagen was launching a new model in a market that had shifted: fewer people were walking into dealerships, and digital was doing more of the consideration work than ever before. We built an AR experience that let prospective buyers place a true-to-scale model of the new VW in their driveway, garage, or street — walk around it, open the doors, configure the colour — from their phone, before the car was even in stock.

The experience was launched through targeted digital media and a QR-enabled OOH campaign in fifteen Canadian cities. Over 120,000 Canadians placed a Volkswagen in their environment within the first six weeks. Dealer inquiry rates in AR-targeted markets were 41% higher than in control markets. The campaign was shortlisted at the One Show and became the global benchmark for VW’s AR launch strategy.
